forces.title: Widespread Generative AI Application Adoption by UK Consumers
forces.description: As of May 2026, 63% of UK consumers have used a Generative AI application like ChatGPT or Google Gemini, a 37% increase from 2025. One in ten consumers uses Gen AI daily, with even higher rates in Greater London (18%). This widespread adoption signifies a strong and rapidly expanding user base for consumer-facing AI applications, providing a robust demand driver for the Application Software segment and indicating high user engagement.

forces.title: Increasing Workplace Adoption of Generative AI for Productivity
forces.description: 14.5 million people in the UK used Generative AI for work in 2026, an increase from 11 million in 2025. Seven million workers are using free Gen AI tools, potentially alongside sanctioned tools. The most common applications are search and emails. This trend highlights a significant and growing demand for enterprise AI application software and productivity tools, driving adoption and creating opportunities for software vendors to monetize and integrate AI into business workflows.

forces.title: Payments Value Shifts to Software-Driven Control Layer
forces.description: The payments industry is undergoing a structural shift where value is relocating from front-end checkout screens to an 'invisible control layer' comprising back-end trust, machine identity, consent engines, and dynamic routing protocols. This shift is driven by checkouts dissolving into software and the rise of agentic payments. Incremental gross profit expansion is increasingly concentrating in the software and workflow layers, leading to higher valuations for providers with deep workflow integration and proprietary interface ownership.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Hyperscaler AI Infrastructure Investment Fuels Cloud Growth
forces.description: Five major hyperscalers have announced significant capital expenditures, totaling approximately $800 billion for 2026 and $1 trillion for 2027, with the vast majority allocated to AI infrastructure. This massive investment in compute, storage, and networking as consumption services directly benefits the Cloud & Internet Infrastructure segment, driving demand and expansion for providers of IaaS/PaaS and systems software within this category. This growth is sustained by the increasing demand for AI models.
forces.source_title: The $2.3 trillion horizon: How AI is rewriting the semiconductor story

forces.title: Rising Data Centre Energy Costs and Semiconductor Constraints
forces.description: The UK computers and telecoms sector faces near-term uncertainty due to higher data-centre energy costs and ongoing semiconductor constraints. Semiconductor shortages could reduce shipments by around 9%. While AI adoption and digital infrastructure investment provide long-term strength, these cost and supply pressures pose a significant headwind, impacting the profitability and operational efficiency of Cloud & Internet Infrastructure providers, particularly those reliant on physical data centres and high-performance hardware.

forces.title: Cybersecurity Concerns Following Major Attacks in 2025
forces.description: Cybersecurity remains a key concern for the UK computers and telecoms sector, particularly following major attacks in 2025. This persistent threat environment means businesses must prioritize robust security measures, driving demand for Cybersecurity solutions. However, it also represents an ongoing operational and reputational risk for software and internet services providers, necessitating continuous investment in advanced protection, threat intelligence, and managed security services to safeguard digital assets and customer trust.

forces.title: Customer Spending Shifts to Measurable Productivity Gains
forces.description: Customer spending in the Software & IT Services sector has become more selective, with budgets increasingly directed towards solutions that deliver measurable productivity gains, automation, or operational efficiency. This structural shift means that providers must clearly demonstrate tangible customer value to secure contracts and maintain growth. Companies offering undifferentiated services or lacking clear ROI will face greater competitive pressure, while those focused on outcomes will outperform.

forces.title: Growing Investment in European AI Application Layer Startups
forces.description: European AI application startups (including those in the UK) are experiencing a significant surge in venture capital funding, with H1 2026 levels reaching 44% of US counterparts, up from 11% in 2018. Funding for vertical AI applications specifically reached 67% of US levels. This increased capital inflow, supported by corporate and US-based investors, fuels innovation and growth within the Application Software segment, enabling startups to scale and compete globally in specialized AI solutions.
forces.source_title: Europe’s new AI edge? The emerging application layer opportunity

forces.title: UK's Position as a Global AI Talent Magnet Strengthens
forces.description: The United Kingdom is reinforcing its position as a global talent magnet for AI professionals, driven by a highly concentrated ecosystem anchored in institutions like Google DeepMind. This strong talent pool provides a crucial advantage for Software & Internet Services companies, particularly those developing AI applications. The availability of skilled engineers and researchers supports innovation, R&D velocity, and the ability to scale complex AI solutions within the UK.
forces.source_title: Europe’s new AI edge? The emerging application layer opportunity

forces.title: University Spinouts Drive Commercialization of AI Research
forces.description: European universities, including those in the UK (e.g., Oxford, Cambridge), are increasingly acting as venture builders, reducing equity demands on spinouts and fostering a more founder-friendly environment. This trend is translating research strength into substantial investor backing and highly valued spinouts in vertical AI applications. This structural advantage channels global talent into scalable innovation ecosystems, providing a steady stream of new companies and technologies for the Application Software segment.
forces.source_title: Europe’s new AI edge? The emerging application layer opportunity

forces.title: AI Application Layer Requires Specialized Talent Profiles
forces.description: The shift towards the AI application layer creates a demand for a different talent profile, moving beyond core compute and research to focus on deployment engineers, knowledge experts, and specialists embedded with customers. These roles are critical for providing the domain specificity and workflow depth required for successful enterprise applications. This structural change necessitates adapted talent strategies for software companies, focusing on upskilling and attracting specialized personnel to meet evolving industry needs.
forces.source_title: Europe’s new AI edge? The emerging application layer opportunity

viewpoints.title: Software & IT Services Remain Attractive Despite Polarized Market Conditions
viewpoints.description: The UK Software and IT services sector is fundamentally attractive and growth-oriented, though recent conditions show increasing polarization. Success hinges on scale, recurring revenue, and AI capability as key differentiators. Customer spending has become more selective, prioritizing solutions offering measurable productivity gains and operational efficiency. Businesses demonstrating clear value propositions and strong retention are outperforming, while less differentiated providers face heightened competition. Long-term prospects are strong, but commercial outcomes from innovation are critical for success.

viewpoints.title: Accelerating AI Adoption and Digital Infrastructure Boost UK Tech Strength
viewpoints.description: The UK computers and telecoms sector, encompassing digital infrastructure, benefits from accelerating AI adoption and sustained investment. This underpins the sector's long-term strength despite near-term uncertainties like higher data-centre energy costs, semiconductor constraints, and rising cyber risks. Public and private investment in AI, digital infrastructure, and skills development, through initiatives like the Digital and Technologies Sector Plan and AI Growth Zones, further supports this resilience.

viewpoints.title: Europe's AI Application Layer Poised for Significant Economic Opportunity
viewpoints.description: As AI adoption matures, the competitive focus in Europe (including the UK) is shifting towards the application layer of the AI tech stack. This layer involves software understanding specific workflows, operating within existing enterprise systems, and automating tasks in complex environments. European companies, with their deep industrial expertise, regulatory rigor, and experience in heterogeneous markets, are uniquely positioned to capture significant economic opportunities by transforming everyday business processes with AI applications.
viewpoints.source_title: Europe’s new AI edge? The emerging application layer opportunity

viewpoints.title: Payments Value Shifting to Software and Workflow Layers
viewpoints.description: Value in the global payments sector is increasingly concentrating in the software and workflow layers surrounding transactions, rather than just transaction processing. This shift is driven by the dissolution of checkouts into software and the rise of invisible, agentic payments. Software-led acquirers and vertical SaaS platforms now derive 40-60% of gross profit from embedded payments, value-added services, and software subscriptions, indicating a more defensible and lucrative margin structure for software providers in this domain.
viewpoints.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

demand_drivers.description: Enterprises are moving beyond model experimentation to redesign legacy business processes, increasing demand for specialized AI software that integrates deeply into workflows.
Significant investment is concentrated in vertical AI applications for complex and regulated sectors, requiring tailored software solutions.
